niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces that feel spacious, clearly structured, and easy to scan, with strong hierarchy, readable text, rounded components, and restrained visual clutter. They frequently favor light or mixed-light surfaces with subtle accents, modular card-based organization, prominent imagery when it supports the task, and controls that are clearly visible but not overly aggressive. They also repeatedly prefer simpler grouping, clearer labels, and layouts that keep attention on one main focal area rather than splitting it across many competing sections.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers open, spacious, breathable layouts with fewer competing elements visible at once, less crowding, and clearer separation between sections.
Prefers strong, obvious hierarchy with a clear focal point, prominent primary content, and well-structured sections that guide attention cleanly.
Prefers content organized into distinct modular cards or clearly separated grouped sections rather than fragmented, continuous, or overly mixed layouts.
Prefers softer rounded cards, pill-shaped controls, and gentler corner radii over squarer, boxier, or harsher component shapes.
Prefers high legibility, straightforward text hierarchy, visible labels, supportive subtitles, and text treatments that are easy to read rather than stylized or low-contrast.
Generally prefers lighter or balanced color themes, muted/subtle accents, and softer contrast over darker, heavier, neon, or overly saturated treatments.
Prefers actions and controls that are explicit, visible, and well organized—such as clear CTAs, labeled inputs, side-by-side or well-spaced buttons, and simple control styling.
